messages.content: Write a polished short scene in modern American English between two adult friends waiting to hear whether a small plan will work out. Nothing dangerous or ominous is happening. Let uncertainty change their behavior and conversation naturally. Avoid suspense language, ominous hints, and artificial stakes.

“Any answer?”

Jordan checked her email again.

“No.”

Alex looked at the clock. “They said by five.”

“It is five.”

“Five-oh-two.”

“Still five.”

Alex smiled. “You're very precise when you're nervous.”

“I'm not nervous.”

“You've checked the same email six times.”

“Seven.”

“Right.”

Jordan put the phone down.

“I just need to know.”

“I know.”

She stood and walked to the kitchen.

“What are you doing?” Alex asked.

“Making coffee.”

“You already had coffee.”

“That was different.”

“How?”

“It was earlier.”

Alex laughed.

Jordan opened the cabinet, then closed it.

“I don't actually want coffee.”

“I figured.”

“Don't sound smug.”

“I wouldn't dare.”

Jordan came back and sat down.

The phone remained on the table.

Five minutes passed.

A notification appeared.

Jordan looked at it.

“It's an ad.”

Alex nodded. “Naturally.”

Jordan picked up the phone again.

“You know what?”

“What?”

“If they don't answer by five-thirty, I'm ordering takeout.”

“That sounds reasonable.”

“And I'm ordering dessert.”

“Now we're planning.”

Jordan smiled.

“See? Problem solved.”
